body:
We should not call constructors from specs, as they can be overridden by user script (e.g. `window.CSSStyleSheet = ...`)

Instead we need to refactor the constructible stylesheets spec. Given recent changes to Web IDL constructors, I think that will look like the following:

- Add a "setup a CSSStyleSheet" algorithm which takes a `CSSStyleSheet` and applies all the sub-bullets of step 1 from [the constructor definition](https://wicg.github.io/construct-stylesheets/#dom-cssstylesheet-cssstylesheet)
- Change [the constructor definition](https://wicg.github.io/construct-stylesheets/#dom-cssstylesheet-cssstylesheet) to apply the "setup a CSSStyleSheet" algorithm to **this**, in place of step 1.
- Change steps 2-3 to refer to **this** instead of _sheet_
- Remove step 4
- In the HTML spec, replace this line with "1. Let _sheet_ be a [new](https://heycam.github.io/webidl/#new) `CSSStyleSheet` in _settings_'s realm. 2. Setup a CSSStyleSheet given _sheet_."

/cc @rakina

body:
There's currently no way to specify module type on the `<script>` element, so only JavaScript modules can be imported using `src` (anything with a non-JS MIME type will continue to fail when imported this way). So I think the statement is correct as-is.

Eventually I think we should add a type attribute to let `<link rel='modulepreload'>` be used to prime the module map for non-JS module types, but that can probably be a separate follow-up.
